question.text: Within how many trading days must an FPI divest excess holdings if it breaches the 10% threshold in a listed company?

answer.text: 5 trading days from the date of settlement of the trades resulting in the breach
10 trading days from the date of settlement of the trades resulting in the breach
15 trading days from the date of settlement of the trades resulting in the breach
3 trading days from the date of the trade resulting in the breach

explanation.text: The Logic: Under Regulation 20(6) of the SEBI (FPI) Regulations, 2019, where the total investment by an FPI together with its investor group reaches or exceeds the 10 per cent threshold of paid-up equity capital of a listed company, the FPI must divest the excess holding within 5 trading days from the date of settlement of the trades resulting in the breach. The Trap: 10 and 15 trading days inflate the divestment window. 3 trading days from the trade date is also incorrect because the clock starts from the settlement date, not the trade date. If the FPI fails to divest within the 5-trading-day window, the entire investment in that company is reclassified as Foreign Direct Investment. Note: Explanation reworded to replace the confusing "exceeds below 10%" phrasing with "reaches or exceeds the 10 per cent threshold", and the role-specific pro-tip label has been removed.
